comment: Both tree treatments exceed the family-repeatability reference 0.10 and the pre-read substantial pair-order reversal reference 1/3; S3, but not prune, reaches the exact strong-reversal threshold of 0.40. Rank portability is strongly positive in K, in contrast with rho.

contrast_with_rho.interpretation: Named trait rankings transfer under K but not under distance-dissimilarity rho in the same trait-by-family graph. The two statistics have different biological meanings, so neither is a substitute for the other.

caveats: A rank-reversal rate of 40–44% is not evidence of biological process heterogeneity by itself; even identical independent Brownian processes give about 50% reversal.
The K family effect may be affected by phylogenetic geometry, species support or source composition. An observed-tree same-process process null is required.
The test is post-outcome; it does not reclassify frozen prospective rho results.
K is standardized relative to Brownian evolution, not a direct evolutionary-rate estimate.
